page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The server contains no integrated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage options for persistent storage needs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core performance, evidenced by elevated results in stress-ng single-core tests (3079.08) and Geekbench single-core processing (1989.0), as well as text processing workloads. Multi-core performance is moderate for a 4-vCPU system, achieving 6154.87 in stress-ng and 4458.0 in Geekbench. Relative memory throughput tests demonstrate lower figures for uncached large-block reads (37.99 GB/sec) and small cached blocks, while write bandwidth remains average. Multi-threaded decompression and clang compilation metrics fall into lower comparative percentiles.

Without local NVMe drives, storage I/O and low-latency database transactions are constrained by remote disk performance, reflected in baseline PassMark database test scores and Redis SET rates. The platform remains cost-efficient for general workloads due to its balanced CPU and memory provisioning. Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is technically suited for static web serving, containerized microservices, enterprise application middleware, and small-model CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of system RAM, driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio across 2 physical cores with symmetric multithreading, the instance includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, using attached remote disks for file operations. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core compute performance and solid text processing throughput, balanced against average multi-core results and modest uncached memory read speeds. Database operations and multi-threaded compilation tasks reflect entry-level performance bounds for this resource class. D4as_v6 is best suited for application backends, container orchestration nodes, static web serving, and lightweight general-purpose cloud workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without local disk overhead.
